success_patterns: First-turn hotel-only or flight+hotel requests with no explicit dates produced a single seek_information naming only the missing items. 'Anniversary', 'last-minute' and '3 people' were treated as context, not dates.

When the user supplied dates after the assistant asked for them, the agent ran search_hotels immediately for the domain with no key. It carried the city and rooms/people from earlier turns, left the cached restaurants key alone, and saved under 'hotels'.

Hotel refinement replies (neighborhood, wifi+gym, balcony, 'Downtown X preferred') were written as a three-line load/filter/save block. The most refined hotels key was loaded (filtered_hotels2, hotels2, or hotels when it was the only one). Only the kwargs from the last message were passed, with no re-passing of rooms, budget or stars already in the summary, and no flight, restaurant or search_nearest lines.
A bare 'That sounds amazing, yes' was mapped to the single amenity the assistant had just proposed (balcony -> has_balcony=True), not to earlier amenities.
A first attraction request with a named city and type was written as an assigned search_attractions(city=..., type=[...]) followed by save_to_cache(key='attractions'), with no extra params.
Save keys were always new, unused names, and every call was assigned and followed by save_to_cache.

patch.reasoning: All eight successes are already covered by the existing skill: the seek_information-only gate, first search once dates arrive, single-domain refinement from the most refined key, the kwarg trace for 'Yes' replies, and the hygiene rules. The optimizer meta-skill says that adding gate text or examples was net-negative, and recent edits to the same rules (Rules 2/17 wording, the -1 flight block, first-search blocks) were rejected for regressions. No success pattern here is uncovered or shared across several trajectories, so any addition would only lengthen the skill and risk attention dilution. The best action is to leave the skill unchanged.
